courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Quantitative Methods for Medical Decision Making
courses.description: The objective of this course is to provide students with a theoretical and practical knowledge of quantitative methods for medical decision-making. We will discuss the basic concepts of real-world evidence, health preferences research, infectious disease modelling methods, and health economics for informing decisions of health policy making. Practical sessions will be provided to equip students with technical skills for solving real-world questions.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health and MSc Epidemiology and Biostatistics
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:

1. apply common methods in analyzing real-world data.
2. understand the concept of health preference research and apply the methods for preference elicitation
3. interpret the common epidemic quantities and apply modelling skills for epidemic control.
4. apply health economic methods for medical decision making
courses.course_syllabus:
| **Topic** | **Contents/fundamental concepts** |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Real-world evidence in medical decision making | * Basic concept of real-world data and common methods in analyzing real-world data |
| 2. Health preference research | * Basic concept of health preference research, preference elicitation methods (e.g., discrete choice experiment), and preference for health-related quality of life with case studies |
| 3. Statistical modelling methods for informing infectious disease control | * Statistical inference of infectious disease parameters and common modelling methods (e.g., compartmental models) with demonstration using excel/R software |
| 4. Health economics | * Basic concept of health economics, econometric analysis in health policy, and cost-effectiveness analysis |
